applies_why: The text weighs a collision between the defender's link and the challenger's own chain read together (D6 vs C1 at Acts 2:30), which is exactly the chain-against-chain collision K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: 'the stating-verse test DG-61 retires... for either side': one reading, it bars any ground of decision that turns on whether a verse or a chain states a claim in its own words, so faulting a chain for not naming Joseph, or for resting on an inference rather than a statement, is barred; the other reading, it bars only the exact move 'no verse states the contrary, so the link stands,' leaving a judge free to note naming gaps and inference-dependence as limits of footing.
why: I adopt the first reading because the CHAIN definition forbids judging a link 'by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word,' and this judge affirms both chains are footed yet grounds the UNDERDETERMINED verdict in precisely such statement-based faults against both sides, which K-C retires for either side.
